title: Dynamics Among Borderline Personality and Anxiety Features in Psychotherapy Outpatients: An Exploration of Nomothetic and Idiographic Patterns
limitations: - Small sample size; - Limited time span (21 days); - Measurement confined to self-report; - Potential for missing data due to non-random intervals; - Lack of robust subgroup structure; - Assumption of weak stationarity may not hold in active treatment settings
notes: The paper does not explicitly state whether the study was preregistered. Code for the analysis is declared available, but data availability is not explicitly stated. The authors used GIMME, which is a novel method for identifying dynamic patterns in EMA data, and the results suggest that symptom dynamics are largely idiographic rather than nomothetic.
